entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Apprehending arrest in connection with Complaint Case No.1168/2023 filed before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate Vaishali, District Hajipur for the offences punishable under Section 498A,
323, 379, 354, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the appellant preferred an application before the High Court seeking anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC for short).

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate Vaishali, District Hajipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Said application for anticipatory bail has been rejected by the High Court vide the impugned order dated 28.03.2025.
Hence, the instant appeal has been preferred.

By order dated 13.05.2025, the following order was passed by this Court:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that permission may be granted to remove the defect(s).
He is permitted to do so.
Issue notice to the respondents, returnable on 30.07.2025.
Learned counsel for the petitioner is permitted to serve the standing counsel for respondent No.1/State.
The parties are at liberty to settle their differences amicably through mediation.
Till the next date of hearing, no coercive steps shall be taken as against the petitioner provided the petitioner cooperates with the investigation.

Heard learned counsel for the appellant in support of the appeal; learned counsel for the first respondent-State;
learned counsel for the second respondent and perused the material on record.

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the offences alleged against the appellant herein are under Sections 498A and other offences under the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961; that these allegations are wholly false and frivolous; however, he has been appearing before the Court and extending his cooperation.
Nevertheless, the appellant has been harassed inasmuch as despite the interim order granted by this Court, the appellant was arrested and subsequently released after ten hours.

Having regard to this episode,
this Court may consider making the interim order absolute and thereby protecting the appellant herein subject to the terms and conditions that may be imposed.

Learned standing counsel for the first respondent-State with reference to the counter- affidavit however contended that there is no merit in this appeal and that the High Court rightly rejected the anticipatory bail to the appellant herein.

Learned counsel for the second respondent also vehemently objected to any relief being granted to the appellant herein as the Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate had issued a non- bailable warrant as against the appellant herein owing to his non-cooperation and therefore, this Court may not grant any relief to him.
We have considered the arguments advanced at the bar.
Considering the circumstances on record, in our view, the appellant is entitled to the relief claimed under Section 438 CRPC.
We, therefore, allow this appeal and set- aside the order passed by the High Court.

We direct that in the event of arrest of the appellant, the Arresting Officer shall release the appellant on bail, subject to furnishing cash security of the sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two like sureties.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the ensuing trial.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty and shall not in any way influence the witnesses or tamper with the material on record.
Any infraction of the conditions may entail cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the appellant.
With the aforesaid directions, the appeal is allowed.
, J ( B . V . N A G A R A T H N A )
, J (UJJAL BHUYAN)
